ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Usher syndrome (USH) is an autosomal recessive genetic disease with impaired hearing and vision, divided into α type, β type, and γ type. It has been found that mutations in at least 10 different genes can each separately cause USH. The same situation also exists in mice. Two pedigrees of α-type USH caused by single-gene mutations are shown in the figure. Question: What is the probability that II-2 of pedigree 1 is a carrier?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Usher syndrome (USH) is an autosomal recessive genetic disease with impaired hearing and vision, divided into α type, β type, and γ type. It has been found that mutations in at least 10 different genes can each separately cause USH. The same situation also exists in mice. Two pedigrees of α-type USH caused by single-gene mutations are shown in the figure. Question: What is the probability that II-2 of pedigree 1 is a carrier?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: Pedigree 1 in the figure shows that in the first generation, I-1 is a normal male square, and I-2 is a normal female circle; they have two sons. In the second generation, II-1 is an affected male black square, and II-2 is a normal male blank square. Then reason: The stem states that USH is an autosomal recessive genetic disease, and that this pedigree is caused by a single-gene mutation. In pedigree 1, phenotypically normal parents have an affected son II-1, so both parents must be carriers, and their genotypes can be denoted as Aa × Aa. The genotype probabilities of their offspring are AA accounting for 1/4, Aa accounting for 1/2, and aa affected accounting for 1/4. II-2 is known from the figure to be phenotypically normal, so aa is excluded, and conditioning is only among AA and Aa. P(II-2 is a carrier | normal) = (1/2) / (3/4) = 2/3.
